live.name: ALPHV
live.headline: ALPHV: a ransomware actor known by several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists ALPHV under several aliases and a set of tools. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: ALPHV is the main name for this actor in the catalogue record.
It is also listed as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
The catalogue links the name to tools including BlackCat, Noberus, Munchkin, Mimikatz, Impacket, PsExec, LaZagne, MEGAsync and GO Simple Tunnel (GOST).
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: ALPHV
next.headline: ALPHV (BlackCat): a ransomware-as-a-service gang with a public run of extortion claims
next.in_short: ALPHV, also called BlackCat, ran a ransomware-as-a-service operation that surfaced in late 2021. Reports tie it to many extortion claims. Its leak sites were disrupted in late 2023, and it was reported to be exit scamming in March 2024.

sentences.t: ALPHV is also tracked as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466, according to the catalogue record.
Sygnia says the BlackCat group surfaced in November 2021 and uses a ransomware-as-a-service model. Cybernews notes the group was known for using the Rust programming language.
BleepingComputer says ALPHV is believed to be a rebrand of the DarkSide and BlackMatter ransomware operations.

BleepingComputer reports the FBI linked the gang to over 60 breaches in its first four months. It also reports a law enforcement estimate of at least $300 million in ransoms from over 1,000 victims up to September 2023.

Victims named in the cards include local governments. DataBreaches reports that BlackCat claimed the 2022 Suffolk County attack, which disabled the county's 911 system. A report on the 2023 Alexandria, Louisiana case says the AlphV gang listed the city as a victim.
Companies are on the list too. AlphV claimed the Henry Schein incident, a report says. BleepingComputer relays the gang's claim of over 1 TB stolen from Constellation Software.
BleepingComputer reports that ALPHV listed loanDepot and Prudential Financial on its leak site. The report says the claims were unverified because the gang had not yet published proof.
Sygnia investigated a 2023 intrusion it attributed to BlackCat or one of its affiliates, not to a single confirmed actor. Access came through a compromised third-party vendor.
In that case the attacker moved through the network for weeks with Cobalt Strike and tunnelling tools. It sent stolen data to cloud storage with Rclone and then emailed extortion threats.
The catalogue lists tools tied to the group, including Mimikatz, PsExec, Impacket, LaZagne and MEGAsync.
Leak-site pressure is a repeated pattern. In the Constellation case, the gang leaked some documents as proof and threatened to release the rest if the company ignored its ransom demand.

In a statement relayed by one article, AlphV said it kept administrator access to MGM's systems. It also said it launched ransomware against more than 100 ESXi hypervisors on September 11. These are the gang's own unverified claims.
DataBreaches describes an unconfirmed claim that AlphV got a Viking Therapeutics employee to file an SEC complaint under the new cyber disclosure rule.
BleepingComputer reports that in December 2023 an international law enforcement operation seized the gang's Tor negotiation and leak sites. It says the FBI had temporarily taken the sites down.

BleepingComputer links the 2024 Change Healthcare attack to BlackCat through unnamed sources, which it could not confirm. UnitedHealth's SEC filing describes a suspected nation-state actor. BlackCat had not claimed the attack when the article was published.

In March 2024 BleepingComputer concluded the gang was pulling an exit scam. Its sites went offline, affiliates said they were not paid, and it offered its source code for $5 million. It posted a fake FBI seizure banner, which Europol and the NCA said they had no part in.
The same report says it is unclear whether the group will return under a new name.
Keep tested backups that attackers cannot reach, and limit what third-party vendors can access on your network.
